```{r}
  dplyr::select(item = Item, element = Element, year = Year, source = Source,
                value = Value, unit = Unit, flag = Flag)

forest_co2 <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(item == "Forest fires", element == "Emissions (CO2)", source == "FAO TIER 1") |>

forest <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(item == "Forest fires", source == "FAO TIER 1",
                element %in% c("Burned Area", "Emissions (CO2)", "Emissions (CH4)"), year >= 2001) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = year, names_from = element, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::rename(Year = year, `Burned area (ha)` = `Burned Area`,
                `CO2 (kt)` = `Emissions (CO2)`, `CH4 (kt)` = `Emissions (CH4)`)

gap <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(item == "Other forest", element == "Emissions (CO2)") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = year, names_from = source, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(`FAO TIER 1`), !is.na(UNFCCC)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = year, `FAO Tier 1 (kt)` = `FAO TIER 1`, `UNFCCC (kt)` = UNFCCC,

burned <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/nfdb/area-burned-by-province.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

share <- burned |>
  dplyr::summarise(bc = sum(hectares[province == "BC"]), canada = sum(hectares), .by = year) |>

bc <- eccc |>
  dplyr::filter(region == "BC") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(share, year, share), by = "year")

trees_uncertainty <- function(ci_half_width) 0.524417 / 1.645006 * ci_half_width

buffer_table <- c(none = 0.25, `1` = 0.20, `2` = 0.15, `3` = 0.20,
                  `1,2` = 0.10, `1,3` = 0.15, `2,3` = 0.10, `1,2,3` = 0.05)

trees_buffer <- function(mitigating = "none", after_reversal = FALSE) {
  buffer_table[[mitigating]] + if (after_reversal) 0.05 else 0
}

kept <- function(ci_half_width, mitigating = "none", after_reversal = FALSE) {
  1 - trees_uncertainty(ci_half_width) - trees_buffer(mitigating, after_reversal)
}

break_even <- function(...) (1 - trees_buffer(...)) / (0.524417 / 1.645006)

crediting_level <- function(x, years) sum(x[years]) / 5

accounts <- national |>
  dplyr::filter(year >= 2012) |>
  dplyr::mutate(reference = year <= 2016)

level_split  <- sum(accounts$human[accounts$reference]) / 5
level_whole  <- sum(accounts$net[accounts$reference]) / 5

credits <- accounts |>
  dplyr::filter(!reference) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = year,
                   `Disaggregated emissions (Mt)` = human,
                   `Disaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(level_split - human, 1),
                   `Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)` = net,
                   `Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(level_whole - net, 1))

split_pos <- credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
whole_pos <- credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
worst <- which.min(credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]])

bc_accounts <- bc |> dplyr::filter(year >= 2012)
bc_level_split <- sum(bc_accounts$human[bc_accounts$year <= 2016]) / 5
bc_level_whole <- sum(bc_accounts$net[bc_accounts$year <= 2016]) / 5

bc_credits <- bc_accounts |>
  dplyr::filter(year >= 2017) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = year,
                   `Burned area share (%)` = round(100 * share, 1),
                   `Disaggregated emissions (Mt)` = round(human, 1),
                   `Disaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(bc_level_split - human, 1),
                   `Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)` = round(net, 1),
                   `Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(bc_level_whole - net, 1))

bc_split_pos <- bc_credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
bc_whole_pos <- bc_credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
bc_worst <- which.min(bc_credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]])

classify <- function(n) {
  base <- forest_co2[forest_co2$year < min(forest_co2$year) + n, ]
  thr <- mean(base$co2) + 2 * stats::sd(base$co2)
  data.frame(`Baseline (years)` = n,
             Period = if (nrow(base) < n) NA_character_ else
               paste(min(base$year), max(base$year), sep = "-"),
             `Threshold (kt)` = if (nrow(base) < n) NA_real_ else round(thr),
             `Years classified natural` = if (nrow(base) < n) "baseline longer than the series" else
               paste(forest_co2$year[forest_co2$co2 > thr], collapse = ", "),
             check.names = FALSE)
}
baselines <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(13, 20, 30), classify))

ci <- c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.50, 2.00)
deductions <- data.frame(
  `Uncertainty, 90% interval half width (%)` = ci * 100,
  `Uncertainty deduction (%)` = round(100 * trees_uncertainty(ci), 1),
  `Kept, 25% buffer (%)` = round(100 * kept(ci), 1),
  `Kept, 5% buffer (%)` = round(100 * kept(ci, "1,2,3"), 1),
  `Kept, 30% buffer after a reversal (%)` = round(100 * kept(ci, after_reversal = TRUE), 1),
  check.names = FALSE)

set.seed(42)
sd_mt <- 16.6 * (44 / 12) / 1.96

simulate_reductions <- function(reference, emissions, n = 10000) {
  level <- rowMeans(matrix(rep(reference, each = n) +
                             stats::rnorm(n * length(reference), 0, sd_mt), nrow = n))
  level - (emissions + stats::rnorm(n, 0, sd_mt))
}

monte_carlo <- function(reference, series) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(series)), function(k) {
    draws <- simulate_reductions(reference, series$emissions[k])
    half <- (stats::quantile(draws, 0.95) - stats::quantile(draws, 0.05)) / 2
    data.frame(Year = series$year[k], mean = mean(draws), half = half,
               ci = half / abs(mean(draws)))
  }))
}

reference_split <- accounts$human[accounts$reference]
reference_whole <- accounts$net[accounts$reference]

mc_split <- monte_carlo(reference_split,
  data.frame(year = credits$Year, emissions = credits[["Disaggregated emissions (Mt)"]]))
mc_whole <- monte_carlo(reference_whole,
  data.frame(year = credits$Year, emissions = credits[["Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)"]]))

blank_if_negative <- function(value, mean_reduction) ifelse(mean_reduction > 0, value, NA)

uncertainty <- data.frame(
  Year = mc_split$Year,
  `Disaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(mc_split$mean, 1),
  `Disaggregated interval (% of mean)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * mc_split$ci), mc_split$mean),
  `Disaggregated deduction (%)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * trees_uncertainty(mc_split$ci), 1), mc_split$mean),
  `Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(mc_whole$mean, 1),
  `Undisaggregated interval (% of mean)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * mc_whole$ci), mc_whole$mean),
  check.names = FALSE)

over <- uncertainty[["Disaggregated deduction (%)"]] > 100
banked <- ifelse(mc_split$mean > 0, 100 * purrr::map2_dbl(mc_split$ci, mc_split$Year > min(credits$Year[!split_pos]), \(ci, after) kept(ci, after_reversal = after)), NA)

msd <- \(x) sprintf("%.1f ± %.1f Mt CO~2~e a year (95 per cent confidence interval %.1f to %.1f)",
                    mean(x), stats::sd(x), stats::t.test(x)$conf.int[1], stats::t.test(x)$conf.int[2])
province <- dplyr::filter(eccc, region == "BC")
```

# Abstract {.unnumbered}

Separating natural disturbance from human activity decided whether Canada and British Columbia could report a creditable forest carbon balance at all in the years of the largest fires on record, rather than merely narrowing the uncertainty of one. The 2019 Refinement to the 2006 guidelines of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change offers that separation as an option and sets no length for the record it requires, and little is known about what it does to the credit a jurisdiction can issue. This study compared two accounts of the same land, one that separates natural disturbance and one that does not, for Canada and for British Columbia across the crediting years 2017 to 2024 against a 2012 to 2016 reference period, using the published components of the national inventory for 1990 to 2024, the fire polygons of the Canadian National Fire Database and the fire emissions of the Food and Agriculture Organization statistical database. The crediting level, the uncertainty deduction and the buffer withholding of the REDD+ Environmental Excellence Standard were implemented as the standard writes them, and the natural disturbance threshold was calibrated on baselines of thirteen, twenty and thirty years. The account Canada reports earned reductions in `r sum(split_pos)` of the `r nrow(credits)` crediting years, totalling `r round(sum(credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][split_pos]), 1)` million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, while the same land without the separation earned them in `r sum(whole_pos)` years and fell `r format(abs(credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][worst]), big.mark = ",")` million tonnes below the crediting level in `r credits$Year[worst]` alone. British Columbia, which held `r bc_credits[["Burned area share (%)"]][bc_credits$Year == 2023]` per cent of the area burned in Canada in 2023, earned `r round(sum(bc_credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][bc_split_pos]), 1)` million tonnes on the separated account and fell `r format(abs(bc_credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][bc_worst]), big.mark = ",")` million tonnes short without it. Lengthening the baseline from thirteen to twenty years raised the threshold that marks a year as natural by `r round(100 * (baselines[["Threshold (kt)"]][2] / baselines[["Threshold (kt)"]][1] - 1))` per cent without changing which years it marked, and the two deductions of the standard leave nothing to issue once reported uncertainty reaches `r round(100 * break_even())` per cent. Carbon standards that credit jurisdictions therefore rest on a separation their own guidance leaves undefined, and the rule that defines it decides the credit.

# Introduction

National greenhouse gas inventories reported the land sector on the assumption that every emission and removal on managed land was caused by people [@kurz2018quantifying], a convention the 2019 Refinement to the IPCC Guidelines called the managed land proxy. In Canada's managed forest that convention joined the effects of harvest and regrowth to those of fire and insects, whose emissions and later removals were large and varied widely from year to year, so that the effect of management on the reported trend was masked [@kurz2018quantifying]. The Refinement took Canada's series for 1990 to 2016 as its example of a country whose year-to-year variation from natural disturbance was much larger than that of the rest of its managed forest, and offered "an approach that countries can apply on a voluntary basis within the MLP in order to indicate those emissions and removals considered to result from human activity, and those that are understood to result from natural disturbances", on the expectation that the carbon dioxide released where natural disturbance struck would "be balanced by subsequent removals across the landscape at some future point in time" [@ogle2019generic].

How much the separation mattered in Canada was known before the Refinement was written. With random future fire and insect outbreaks taken into account, the Carbon Budget Model of the Canadian Forest Sector projected Canada's managed forest as a source of 30 to 245 Mt CO~2~e a year during the first commitment period of the Kyoto Protocol, 2008 to 2012, a range equal to nearly 30 per cent of the country's emissions in 2005, and the impact of natural disturbance was among the reasons Canada chose not to elect forest management under the Protocol [@kurz2008risk]. The outbreak of mountain pine beetle in British Columbia was expected to turn the province's forest into a net source by 2020, which led to the argument that later agreements should protect the incentive to manage forests against the effects of natural disturbance [@teobaldelli2008natural]. A forecast to 2100 gave the managed forest an annual probability of being a sink after 2050 near 70 per cent if the area burned stayed at its level of the late twentieth century and 35 per cent if it rose, and every simulation produced a cumulative source over 2010 to 2100 [@metsaranta2010implications]. Canada's own implementation, introduced in its 2017 inventory, split the managed forest into land dominated by natural disturbance and the remaining managed forest, whose fluxes summed to the net emissions and removals of the whole [@kurz2018quantifying], and moved an area from the first part to the second once the stand had grown back to the age at which it held enough wood to be worth cutting, 60 years for the whole country in 2017 [@kurz2018quantifying] and later between 60 and 100 years depending on the region [@kurz2024revised]. The split mattered to the reported balance rather than to the atmosphere. Revising the record of what was harvested between 1889 and 1989 moved 34 million hectares out of the managed part in 1990 and cut the sink reported as human caused by 113 Mt CO~2~e in that year, 56 per cent of it, and by 30 Mt CO~2~e in 2021, 23 per cent of it [@kurz2024revised]. Read from the inventory's own tables, forestry in Canada was a net source of 90.8 Mt CO~2~e a year from 2005 to 2021 while the inventory reported a sink of 4.7 Mt CO~2~e a year, a difference the authors explained by Canada's treatment of wildfire emissions as natural [@bysouth2024high].

Other countries reached the separation by other routes. The United States adopted an accounting framework that divided the change in forest carbon among growth, land use change and natural disturbances such as fire [@woodall2015forest], and Australia classified a whole fire season as natural when national fire emissions exceeded the mean of a 2000 to 2012 baseline by two standard deviations and a state's burned area exceeded its own baseline mean by one standard deviation [@bowman2023wildfire]. The difference between the routes became visible as disturbance rose. Every dataset compared across Europe agreed that forest carbon uptake in 2020 to 2023 was 17 to 27 per cent below its average for 1990 to 2019 [@linscheid2026forest], and a projection from country reports and satellite maps of disturbance, released as a preprint, put the fall in the forest sink of the 27 countries of the European Union at 44 per cent by 2030, driven by disturbance outpacing regrowth [@ritter2025alarming]. For North America in 2010 to 2019 the inventories reported a net source of 7,270 Tg CO~2~e a year against 6,132 Tg from atmospheric inversions and 9,060 Tg from process models, and part of the difference came from what each counted as human or natural, the managed land proxy included [@poulter2026north]. Countries together reported a net land sink of 1.6 Gt CO~2~ a year over 2000 to 2020 where the FAOSTAT dataset estimated a net source of 1.1 Gt CO~2~ [@grassi2022carbon], and in the tropics the net emissions of forestry and other land use for 2011 to 2018 ran from 5.47 Gt CO~2~ a year in one bookkeeping model to 3.21 Gt in FAOSTAT and 1.17 Gt in the national inventories [@nyawira2024pantropical].

The separation had a policy history older than the Refinement. Factoring out natural and indirect human effects from direct human ones was seen in the Kyoto period as a requirement of any accounting that tied credits and debits clearly to human activity, and @canadell2007factoring set out five ways to do it, longer accounting or measurement periods to reduce the effect of year-to-year variation, correction of national inventories for that variation, activity-based accounting with carbon response curves, national baselines or benchmarks, and stratification of the landscape into units with distinct average carbon stocks, while judging demographic and process-based models too demanding of data for an inclusive international system at the time. The same period examined the factoring out of past disturbance and management carried in the age-class structure of a forest [@bottcher2008accounting] and whether natural sinks could be excluded when the estimates of a sink were verified [@alexandrov2004verification]. A review of the rules from Kyoto to Paris concluded that "factoring out direct human-induced from indirect human-induced and natural impacts on managed lands" was among the core requirements "not sufficiently secured by currently discussed accounting rules" [@krug2018accounting], and the forest reference levels of the European Union were shown with the Carbon Budget Model to have credited harvest increases that policy assumed and that never took place [@grassi2018science].

Canada's figures came from one model. The Carbon Budget Model of the Canadian Forest Sector, CBM-CFS3, was the core of Canada's National Forest Carbon Monitoring, Accounting and Reporting System, a spatially referenced Tier 3 approach built on the gain and loss method of the IPCC, which grew each stand along an empirical yield curve, reset its age to zero after a disturbance that replaced the stand, and moved its carbon among pools, to the atmosphere and to forest products through a disturbance matrix specific to each type of disturbance [@kurz2018quantifying]. Tested against 71 years of reconstructed growth and disturbance on a 62 km^2^ boreal landscape in eastern Canada, the model underestimated the net biomass gain of undisturbed stands by 10 per cent [@bernier2010reconstructing]. Its fire matrices assumed that every fire burned at high severity, and a sub-model that related field measurements of biomass consumption to satellite maps of burn severity found that the existing approach gave regional emissions typically 10 to 25 per cent higher, because fires of mixed severity consumed less of the canopy [@thompson2026incorporating]. Applied in Europe, the same model put the forest management sink of the European Union at 365 Mt CO~2~ a year for 2000 to 2012, about 8 per cent below the inventories [@pilli2016modellingb], matched the inventories of 26 countries well in nine and partly in ten, with the mismatches traced to how year-to-year variation, the pools other than biomass and the carbon dioxide from fire were represented [@pilli2016modellinga], and reduced Italy's sink for 2000 to 2009 from 23.7 to 20.5 Mt CO~2~ a year once fire was added to the simulation [@pilli2013application]. A review of 426 articles on forest carbon in Canada published from 2012 to 2021 found the inventory's treatment of human influence and natural disturbance at the centre of that work, and a divide between the models used for management and those used for research [@smyth2024year].

Whether a fire year counted as natural depended on the statistics of the fire regime, a field older than any inventory. Under random periodic fire the expected age-class structure of a forest was the negative exponential distribution, so that "the present age-class structure of such a forest is the key to its past fire history" [@wagner1978class], and the negative exponential and Weibull models became the standard descriptions of fire history [@johnson1985theory], with the fire cycle defined as the time required to burn an area equal to the area studied [@johnson1991climatically]. These statistics were the largest single body of work the review charted, and the fire cycles it reported for Canada ran from 50 years before 1730 and 90 years after it in the Kananaskis watershed of Alberta [@johnson1991climatically] to 229 years over the last 300 in eastern Canada [@cyr2016quantifying], 247 years for 1734 to 2009 in the black spruce forest of central Quebec [@belisle2011fire] and 769 years in Newfoundland [@arsenault2016unravelling]. The estimates depended on how much record was used. Changing the length of a Landsat series in Portugal from 22 to 31 years substantially changed the fitted Weibull parameters [@oliveira2011fire], parametric estimates of the fire cycle were degraded by short-term variation in fire activity [@cyr2016quantifying], the accuracy of Weibull fire intervals fell as the record of fire scars degraded [@parsons2007assessing], and tests of the negative exponential fit could falsely reject it, and so suggest that fire frequency had changed, because the old tail of the age distribution was censored [@finney1995missing]. A normal fire year was defined, by analogy with climate normals, from the 26-year means of fire frequency, area burned and severity around Yosemite [@lutz2011fire], while records of charcoal spanning millennia were put forward as the baseline wherever recent fires were too few to describe the historical range of variability [@gavin2007forest]. In British Columbia the age-class distribution of a sub-boreal landscape gave a stand-replacing fire cycle of 80 to 100 years and lacked stability [@andison2009managing], and disturbance by fire and mountain pine beetle in a study area of 1 million hectares in the central interior was less frequent in 1954 to 2004 than in 1904 to 1953 [@campbell2011natural].

The uncertainty attached to the reported balance was bounded by the method used to combine it. The simple propagation of the 2019 Refinement, its Approach 1, "theoretically requires that the standard deviation divided by the mean value is less than 0.3", and Monte Carlo simulation, its Approach 2, "will be particularly appropriate to use when uncertainties are large, their distribution are non-Gaussian, and algorithms are complex functions" [@paciornik2019uncertainties]. Neither approach prevented an uncertainty larger than the estimate it described, because the percentage was the interval divided by the reported value, and the guidance said so itself, that "caution should be exercised in the interpretation of the results in cases where the point estimate is very small when compared with the size of the confidence interval (e.g. a sector or inventory where removals and emissions are of similar sizes)" [@paciornik2019uncertainties]. Its own worked example for Finland printed ±150 per cent for wetlands remaining wetlands against ±30 per cent for forest land remaining forest land. Regional carbon budgets met the same limit. Australia's land took up a net 36 ± 29 Tg C a year over 1990 to 2011 [@haverd2013australian], the Brazilian Amazon was −59 ± 160 Tg C a year from bottom-up estimates and +36 ± 125 Tg C a year from atmospheric inversions over 2010 to 2018, near neutral given the uncertainty of both [@rosan2023contemporary], and a model of California's land found the uncertainty of its data too high to determine whether the land was a source or a sink, although the effect of management measured against a baseline was valid [@divittorio2021quantifying]. The Monte Carlo interval of Canada's own model was 32.2 Tg C a year wide, an interval that @metsaranta2017uncertainty stated "cannot be meaningfully expressed in percentage terms because its range of possible values contains zero".

The fire emissions a government reached for first were those of FAOSTAT, which the IPCC recommended for checking the activity data and emission estimates of a national inventory. Its Emissions from Fires domain covered 1990 to 2024 for every country, and its methodological note gave the equation, emissions equal to burned biomass multiplied by a default emission factor, and named each input, the MODIS MCD64A1 Collection 6.1 burned area product, the MODIS MCD12Q1 land cover product and the default values of the 2006 IPCC Guidelines [@fao2025fires]. It did not give the code that ran in Google Earth Engine, the rule that allocated a fuel consumption value to each pixel through the ecological and climate zone layers, or the effect of keeping "only those pixels with a percentage uncertainty lower than 20 percent" [@fao2025fires]. It also set the burned area and emissions of fires in organic soils to zero for every country outside Southeast Asia, publishing the full values separately in a table named `AllFires_OrganicSoils.csv` [@fao2025fires]. Independent estimates of fire emissions disagreed widely. Four satellite burned area datasets for Siberia differed by up to fivefold, and the official Russian figures were typically less than 10 per cent of the satellite estimates [@kukavskaya2013fire]. The fires of 2022 in France emitted 7.95 Mt CO~2~e once smouldering combustion in the soil was counted, twice the 4.18 Mt of the global GFAS estimate [@vallet2025soil], and global datasets given the same burned area as a fire-by-fire estimate of the Kilmore East fire in Victoria came out 15 to 37 per cent lower, because they underestimated the fuel consumed [@surawski2016estimates]. The national inventories of the five southern European countries most affected by fire estimated burnt biomass by different methods, and those based on nominal rates of biomass loss could overstate or understate it [@chiriaco2013comparison]. The IPCC Tier 1 defaults applied to the world's forests gave results that differed by about 40 per cent between the guidance of 2003 and that of 2006 [@petrescu2012global], and the United States reported 129 Tg CO~2~ from forest fires in 2022 from a system of its own, the Wildland Fire Emissions Inventory System [@smith2024application].

What the separation was worth was set by the crediting standard rather than by the inventory. Under the REDD+ Environmental Excellence Standard a jurisdiction could leave natural disturbance out of its accounts on exactly the authority described above, since the standard stated that "only anthropogenic emissions shall be considered, and IPCC guidance shall be adhered to on any exclusion of non-anthropogenic emissions", and its 2025 draft adds that natural disturbances "may be excluded if they are 'non-anthropogenic events or non-anthropogenic circumstances that cause significant emissions and are beyond the control of, and not materially influenced by a country'", citing Volume 4, Chapter 2 of the 2019 Refinement [@art2021trees; @art2025trees3; @ogle2019generic]. Two deductions then scaled off whatever the accounts reported. The uncertainty deduction was the gross reductions and removals multiplied by an adjustment factor, 0.524417 divided by 1.645006 and multiplied by the half width of the 90 per cent confidence interval, which the standard required to be estimated by Monte Carlo simulation at 10,000 iterations. The buffer withholding was the same gross quantity multiplied by a contribution of 25 per cent, which fell to 5 per cent where three mitigating factors were met and rose by 5 percentage points for five years after a reversal [@art2021trees]. A reversal retired buffer credits equal to the lower of the emissions above the crediting level or every credit the jurisdiction had been issued.

Other programmes set their reserve against reversal in other ways. The buffer guidelines of the Forest Carbon Partnership Facility set aside 10 to 40 per cent of each period's emission reductions against reversal, of which exposure to fire, storms and drought contributed 5, 3 or 0 percentage points according to whether the risk was judged high, medium or low, and took a separate set-aside for uncertainty that rose in steps to 15 per cent for an aggregate uncertainty above 100 per cent [@fcpf2024buffer]. Verra's tool for projects converted a risk rating into the buffer percentage, with a minimum of 12 and a failure above 60, and scored natural risk from the number of events in the project area over the last 100 years and the share of the carbon stock a single event would remove, extrapolating where data covered at least 20 years but fewer than 100 [@verra2024nprt]. A global analysis released as a preprint estimated the chance of a reversal within 100 years at 31 to 42 per cent, highest in North American conifer forests, tropical rainforests and Asian tropical and subtropical dry forests, and observed that most buffer pools did not vary through space [@wu2026global]. A gridded dataset prepared for the carbon removals regulation of the European Union set each buffer contribution as the mean plus one standard deviation of the modelled loss to disturbance, with a minimum of 10 per cent [@marinelli2026risk], and a review of disturbance risk to forest carbon in the United States concluded that "disturbance risks must be accounted for in carbon offset protocols" [@dye2024carbon].

None of the works this review charted carried a jurisdiction's forest account through the deductions of a crediting standard both with and without the separation of natural disturbance. The nearest were comparisons of Canada's reported series under different partitions [@kurz2024revised; @bysouth2024high], comparisons of national inventories with independent estimates [@pilli2016modellinga; @grassi2022carbon], and maps of reversal risk and buffer contributions made without reference to an inventory [@wu2026global; @marinelli2026risk]. This study therefore aimed to test the natural disturbance approach introduced in the 2019 Refinement to the IPCC Guidelines, by comparing what Canada and British Columbia reported, and what they could have been credited, with and without it over 1990 to 2024, the period of the 2026 national inventory, and to test whether the fire emissions FAOSTAT published could be rebuilt from its stated method and the IPCC Tier 1 steps it cited. It had three objectives.

1. To compare the net emissions of the two accounts for 1990 to 2024, and the reductions, the uncertainty estimated by the Monte Carlo approach of the 2019 Refinement and the buffer of each, under the REDD+ Environmental Excellence Standard for 2017 to 2024.
2. To test how a baseline of 13, 20 or 30 years, a length the 2019 Refinement left unstated, changed the threshold and the years classed as natural, and to show where the regrowth period and a net near zero made the separation hard to apply.
3. To rebuild the forest fire emissions FAOSTAT published for Canada from its stated method and the IPCC Tier 1 steps it cited, and to compare them with what Canada reported.

# Materials and Methods

## Literature review

The literature behind the Introduction and the Discussion was mapped by a scoping review that followed the five stages of @arksey2005scoping as refined by @levac2010scoping and @peters2020updated, reported against the extension of the PRISMA checklist for scoping reviews [@tricco2018prisma]. The review questions, their search strings and the rules for what would change each claim were written into a protocol and committed before the first query ran, and the search terms were drawn only from the title, subtitle and keywords this manuscript carried on 22 October 2026, so that every term could be traced to them. Each search ran from the chunks below and wrote what it found to a file, so that a later render read the files rather than the services.

```{r}
#| label: review-terms
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("04.references/review/search-terms.csv")) {
  front <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE))
  small <- c("a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "by", "do", "does", "for", "from", "how", "in", "into", "is", "its", "of", "on", "or", "the", "to", "under", "using", "versus", "what", "why", "with")
  phrases <- \(x) x |>
    stringr::str_to_lower() |>
    stringr::str_remove_all("[*_]") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("[^[:alnum:][:space:]-]", " | ") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all(paste0("\\b(", paste(small, collapse = "|"), ")\\b"), " | ") |>
    stringr::str_split_1("\\|") |>
    stringr::str_squish() |>
    purrr::keep(\(p) nchar(p) > 2)
  dir.create("04.references/review", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(term = stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_to_lower(unlist(front$keywords))), source = "keywords"),
    tibble::tibble(term = phrases(front$title), source = "title"),
    tibble::tibble(term = phrases(front$subtitle %||% ""), source = "subtitle")
  ) |>
    dplyr::distinct(term, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(question = NA, concept = NA) |>
    readr::write_csv("04.references/review/search-terms.csv", na = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-queries
#| echo: true

front <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE))
declared <- paste(front$title, front$subtitle, paste(unlist(front$keywords), collapse = " ")) |>
  stringr::str_remove_all("[*_]") |>
  stringr::str_to_lower()
term_regex <- \(x) if (stringr::str_ends(x, "\\*")) paste0("\\b", stringr::str_escape(stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$"))) else paste0("\\b", stringr::str_escape(x), "\\b")
terms <- readr::read_csv("04.references/review/search-terms.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(question), !is.na(concept)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(term = stringr::str_to_lower(term)) |>
  tidyr::separate_longer_delim(question, " ")
stray <- terms$term[!purrr::map_lgl(terms$term, \(x) stringr::str_detect(declared, term_regex(x)))]
if (nrow(terms) == 0) stop("No search terms selected in 04.references/review/search-terms.csv")
if (length(stray) > 0) stop("Not in the title, subtitle or keywords: ", paste(unique(stray), collapse = ", "))
queries <- terms |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = c(question, concept), group = paste(term, collapse = "|")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = question, route = paste(c(dplyr::first(question), concept), collapse = "-"), concepts = paste(group, collapse = " AND "))
record_id <- \(doi, title) dplyr::coalesce(stringr::str_to_lower(doi), stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_replace_all(title, "[^[:alnum:] ]", " "))))
```

```{r}
#| label: review-store
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("02.inputs/derived/review-store-hits.csv")) {
  dir.create("02.inputs/derived", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  # library-science manifest, https://github.com/seamusrobertmurphy/library-science/blob/main/library/manifest.csv
  manifest <- readr::read_csv("../library-science/library/manifest.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
  # library-science source notes, https://github.com/seamusrobertmurphy/library-science/tree/main/sources
  notes <- tibble::tibble(path = list.files("../library-science/sources", "\\.md$", full.names = TRUE)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(key = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(path)), note = purrr::map_chr(path, \(p) paste(readLines(p, warn = FALSE), collapse = " ")))
  store <- manifest |>
    dplyr::filter(status %in% c("verified", "filed", "unverified"), !is.na(title) | !is.na(key)) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(notes, key, note), by = "key") |>
    dplyr::mutate(text = stringr::str_to_lower(paste(title, note)))
  hits <- queries |>
    purrr::pmap(\(question, route, concepts) {
      groups <- stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND ")
      term <- \(x) if (stringr::str_ends(x, "\\*")) paste0(stringr::str_escape(stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$")), "\\w*") else paste0(stringr::str_escape(x), "\\b")
      patterns <- purrr::map_chr(groups, \(g) paste0("\\b(", paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), term), collapse = "|"), ")"))
      keep <- purrr::map(patterns, \(r) stringr::str_detect(store$text, r)) |> purrr::reduce(`&`)
      store[keep, ] |> dplyr::transmute(question, route = paste0("store-", route), key, doi, title, year, venue = container, source_note = dplyr::if_else(has_source_note == "yes", key, NA))
    }) |>
    purrr::list_rbind()
  readr::write_csv(hits, "02.inputs/derived/review-store-hits.csv")
  queries |>
    dplyr::transmute(strand = "library-science", route = paste0("store-", route), query = concepts, date = as.character(Sys.Date())) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::count(hits, route, name = "retrieved"), by = "route") |>
    dplyr::mutate(retrieved = tidyr::replace_na(retrieved, 0L), reported_total = retrieved, cap = NA, capped = FALSE, error = NA) |>
    readr::write_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-log-store.csv", na = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-openalex
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("02.inputs/derived/review-openalex-hits.csv")) {
  search_openalex <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 2000) {
    query <- stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND ") |>
      purrr::map_chr(\(g) paste0("(", paste0('"', stringr::str_remove(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), "\\*$"), '"', collapse = " OR "), ")")) |>
      paste(collapse = " AND ")
    tryCatch({
      works <- list(); page <- 1; total <- NA
      repeat {
        # OpenAlex works, searched on title and abstract, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/search-works
        body <- httr2::request("https://api.openalex.org/works") |>
          httr2::req_url_query(filter = paste0("title_and_abstract.search:", query), `per-page` = 200, page = page,
                               select = "doi,title,publication_year,primary_location,type,cited_by_count,abstract_inverted_index") |>
          httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 8, is_transient = \(r) httr2::resp_status(r) == 429, backoff = \(i) 15 * i) |>
          httr2::req_perform() |>
          httr2::resp_body_json()
        total <- body$meta$count
        works <- c(works, body$results)
        Sys.sleep(3)
        if (length(body$results) < 200 || length(works) >= min(total, cap)) break
        page <- page + 1
      }
      hits <- works |>
        purrr::map(\(w) tibble::tibble(doi = stringr::str_remove(w$doi %||% NA_character_, "^https://doi.org/"), title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$publication_year %||% NA_integer_,
                                       venue = w$primary_location$source$display_name %||% NA_character_, type = w$type %||% NA_character_, citations = w$cited_by_count %||% NA_integer_,
                                       abstract = if (length(w$abstract_inverted_index) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(rep(names(w$abstract_inverted_index), lengths(w$abstract_inverted_index))[order(unlist(w$abstract_inverted_index))], collapse = " "))) |>
        purrr::list_rbind() |>
        dplyr::mutate(question, route = paste0("oa-", route), .before = 1)
      list(hits = hits, log = tibble::tibble(strand = "openalex", route = paste0("oa-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = nrow(hits), reported_total = total, cap, capped = total > cap, error = NA))
    }, error = \(e) list(hits = NULL, log = tibble::tibble(strand = "openalex", route = paste0("oa-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = 0L, reported_total = NA, cap, capped = FALSE, error = conditionMessage(e))))
  }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(queries, search_openalex)
  hits <- purrr::map(runs, "hits") |> purrr::list_rbind()
  dir.create("02.inputs/review/raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  hits |>
    dplyr::transmute(id = record_id(doi, title), abstract) |>
    dplyr::distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    readr::write_csv("02.inputs/review/raw/review-abstracts.csv", na = "")
  readr::write_csv(dplyr::select(hits, -abstract), "02.inputs/derived/review-openalex-hits.csv", na = "")
  readr::write_csv(purrr::map(runs, "log") |> purrr::list_rbind(), "02.inputs/derived/review-log-openalex.csv", na = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-semantic-scholar
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("02.inputs/derived/review-s2-hits.csv")) {
  search_s2 <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 3000) {
    query <- stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND ") |>
      purrr::map_chr(\(g) paste0("(", paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), \(x) if (grepl(" ", x)) paste0('"', stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$"), '"') else x), collapse = " | "), ")")) |>
      paste(collapse = " + ")
    tryCatch({
      papers <- list(); token <- NULL; total <- NA
      repeat {
        # Semantic Scholar Academic Graph bulk search, https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/graph#tag/Paper-Data/operation/get_graph_paper_bulk_search
        body <- httr2::request("https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search/bulk") |>
          httr2::req_url_query(query = query, fields = "title,year,venue,externalIds,citationCount,publicationTypes", token = token) |>
          httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 4) |>
          httr2::req_perform() |>
          httr2::resp_body_json()
        total <- body$total; token <- body$token
        papers <- c(papers, body$data)
        if (is.null(token) || length(papers) >= cap) break
      }
      works <- papers |>
        purrr::map(\(w) tibble::tibble(doi = w$externalIds$DOI %||% NA_character_, title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$year %||% NA_integer_, venue = w$venue %||% NA_character_, type = paste(unlist(w$publicationTypes), collapse = " "), citations = w$citationCount %||% NA_integer_)) |>
        purrr::list_rbind()
      list(hits = dplyr::mutate(works, question, route = paste0("s2-", route), .before = 1),
           log = tibble::tibble(strand = "semantic-scholar", route = paste0("s2-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = nrow(works), reported_total = total, cap, capped = total > cap, error = NA))
    }, error = \(e) list(hits = NULL, log = tibble::tibble(strand = "semantic-scholar", route = paste0("s2-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = 0L, reported_total = NA, cap, capped = FALSE, error = conditionMessage(e))))
  }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(queries, search_s2)
  readr::write_csv(purrr::map(runs, "hits") |> purrr::list_rbind() |> dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(question = character(), route = character(), doi = character(), title = character())), "02.inputs/derived/review-s2-hits.csv", na = "")
  readr::write_csv(purrr::map(runs, "log") |> purrr::list_rbind(), "02.inputs/derived/review-log-s2.csv", na = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-chase
#| echo: true

central <- c()
if (length(central) > 0 && !file.exists("02.inputs/derived/review-chase-hits.csv")) {
  chase <- function(seed_doi, direction) {
    # Semantic Scholar Academic Graph references and citations, https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/graph#tag/Paper-Data
    resp <- httr2::request(paste0("https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/DOI:", seed_doi, "/", direction)) |>
      httr2::req_url_query(fields = "title,year,venue,externalIds", limit = 1000) |>
      httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 6) |>
      httr2::req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |>
      httr2::req_perform()
    if (httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200) return(tibble::tibble(seed = seed_doi, route = paste0("chase-", direction), error = httr2::resp_status_desc(resp)))
    key <- if (direction == "references") "citedPaper" else "citingPaper"
    httr2::resp_body_json(resp)$data |>
      purrr::map(\(w) tibble::tibble(doi = w[[key]]$externalIds$DOI %||% NA_character_, title = w[[key]]$title %||% NA_character_, year = w[[key]]$year %||% NA_integer_, venue = w[[key]]$venue %||% NA_character_)) |>
      purrr::list_rbind() |>
      dplyr::mutate(seed = seed_doi, route = paste0("chase-", direction), .before = 1)
  }
  tidyr::expand_grid(seed_doi = central, direction = c("references", "citations")) |>
    purrr::pmap(chase) |>
    purrr::list_rbind() |>
    readr::write_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-chase-hits.csv")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-screening
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("02.inputs/derived/review-screening.csv")) {
  records <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"))
  # Decisions on title and abstract by a language model, one row for each record in each pass, committed with the protocol
  # The pilot pass read the author's 53 records blind under the first rule, the validation pass read 26 of them blind under the revised rule, and the screen pass read the rest
  model <- readr::read_csv("04.references/review/screening-model.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"))
  # The author's decisions, entered by hand in the reading copy of review-records.csv that carries the abstracts, outside git
  # Excel opened that copy as Mac Roman, so the accented characters in its ids are converted back to UTF-8 before the join
  from_mac <- \(x) { y <- iconv(x, "UTF-8", "MACINTOSH"); Encoding(y) <- "UTF-8"; dplyr::coalesce(y, x) }
  by_hand <- readxl::read_excel("02.inputs/review/raw/screening-with-abstracts.xlsx", col_types = "text") |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = from_mac(id))
  stopifnot(setequal(by_hand$id, records$id), setequal(c(by_hand$id[!is.na(by_hand$decision)], model$id[model$pass == "screen"]), records$id))
  screening <- dplyr::select(by_hand, id, author = decision) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::filter(model, pass %in% c("pilot", "screen")) |> dplyr::select(id, model = decision, reason, note), by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(screener = dplyr::if_else(is.na(author), "model", "author"), decision = dplyr::coalesce(author, model), reason = dplyr::if_else(decision == "exclude", reason, NA)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, decision, reason, screener, author, note)
  readr::write_csv(screening, "02.inputs/derived/review-screening.csv", na = "")
  wb <- openxlsx::loadWorkbook("02.inputs/review/raw/screening-with-abstracts.xlsx")
  openxlsx::writeData(wb, 1, dplyr::select(screening, decision, reason), startCol = 8)
  openxlsx::writeData(wb, 1, dplyr::select(screening, screener, note), startCol = 11)
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, "02.inputs/review/raw/screening-with-abstracts.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
}
screening <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-screening.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: review-fulltext
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("02.inputs/derived/review-fulltext.csv")) {
  squash <- \(x) stringr::str_remove_all(stringr::str_to_lower(stringi::stri_trans_general(x, "NFKC; Latin-ASCII")), "[^a-z0-9]")
  # library-science manifest, https://github.com/seamusrobertmurphy/library-science/blob/main/library/manifest.csv
  held_doi <- stringr::str_to_lower(stats::na.omit(readr::read_csv("../library-science/library/manifest.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)$doi))
  # PDFs saved by hand into library-science staging, named by author, year and title, outside git
  staged <- squash(stringr::str_remove(basename(list.files("../library-science/library/staging", "\\.pdf$", recursive = TRUE)), "^.*?\\b(19|20)[0-9]{2}\\b"))
  staged <- substr(staged[nchar(staged) >= 25], 1, 40)
  wanted <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |>
    dplyr::select(id, doi, title, year, routes, url) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::filter(screening, decision %in% c("include", "undecided")) |> dplyr::select(id, decision), by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(work = squash(title),
                  held = dplyr::case_when(routes == "grey" ~ "04.references/literature", stringr::str_to_lower(doi) %in% held_doi ~ "library-science pdf",
                                          purrr::map_lgl(work, \(t) any(startsWith(t, staged))) ~ "library-science staging")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(.by = work, held = dplyr::first(held[!is.na(held)]), copy = dplyr::row_number() > 1)
  todo <- dplyr::filter(wanted, is.na(held), !copy)
  look_up <- function(doi, title) {
    req <- if (!is.na(doi)) {
      # OpenAlex work by DOI, a single-work lookup that costs nothing against the daily budget, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/get-a-single-work
      httr2::request(paste0("https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:", doi))
    } else {
      # OpenAlex works searched by title for a record with no DOI, at $0.001 of the $0.10 a day the unkeyed service allows, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/search-works
      httr2::request("https://api.openalex.org/works") |>
        httr2::req_url_query(filter = paste0("title.search:", stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_replace_all(stringi::stri_trans_nfkc(title), "[^[:alnum:]]", " "))), `per-page` = 5)
    }
    w <- req |> httr2::req_url_query(select = "title,authorships,best_oa_location,locations") |> httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 4) |> httr2::req_perform() |> httr2::resp_body_json()
    if (is.na(doi)) w <- purrr::detect(w$results, \(r) squash(r$title %||% "") == squash(title))
    list(urls = unique(stats::na.omit(c(w$best_oa_location$pdf_url %||% NA, purrr::map_chr(w$locations, \(l) l$pdf_url %||% NA)))),
         authors = purrr::map_chr(w$authorships, \(a) a$author$display_name %||% NA))
  }
  folder <- file.path("../library-science/library/staging", paste0("ipcc-uncertainties-", Sys.Date()))
  dir.create(folder, showWarnings = FALSE)
  fetch <- function(id, doi, title, year, ...) {
    found <- look_up(doi, title)
    Sys.sleep(0.5)
    author <- stringr::word(found$authors[1], -1)
    name <- paste0(dplyr::coalesce(author, "Anon"), if (length(found$authors) > 2) " et al" else "", " ", year, " ",
                   stringr::str_trunc(stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_replace_all(title, "[[:cntrl:]:/\\\\?*\"<>|]", " ")), 120, ellipsis = ""), ".pdf")
    if (file.exists(file.path(folder, name))) name <- sub("\\.pdf$", paste0(" ", substr(rlang::hash(id), 1, 6), ".pdf"), name)
    status <- "no open copy found"
    for (u in found$urls) {
      resp <- tryCatch(httr2::request(u) |> httr2::req_user_agent("ipcc-uncertainties literature review, R httr2") |> httr2::req_timeout(90) |>
                         httr2::req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |> httr2::req_perform(), error = \(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(resp)) { status <- "no answer from the open copy"; next }
      body <- if (httr2::resp_has_body(resp)) httr2::resp_body_raw(resp) else raw()
      if (httr2::resp_status(resp) == 200 && length(body) > 10000 && identical(body[1:4], charToRaw("%PDF"))) {
        writeBin(body, file.path(folder, name))
        return(tibble::tibble(id, author, status = "downloaded", pdf_url = u, file = name))
      }
      status <- if (httr2::resp_status(resp) == 200) "open copy is a web page, not a PDF" else paste("publisher refused,", httr2::resp_status(resp))
    }
    tibble::tibble(id, author, status, pdf_url = found$urls[1], file = NA_character_)
  }
  got <- purrr::pmap(dplyr::select(todo, id, doi, title, year), \(...) tryCatch(fetch(...), error = \(e) tibble::tibble(id = list(...)$id, author = NA_character_, status = paste("lookup failed,", conditionMessage(e)), pdf_url = NA_character_, file = NA_character_)), .progress = TRUE) |>
    purrr::list_rbind()
  log <- wanted |>
    dplyr::left_join(got, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(status = dplyr::case_when(!is.na(held) ~ paste("held in", held), copy ~ "copy of a work listed above", .default = status)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, doi, author, title, year, decision, status, url, pdf_url, file)
  readr::write_csv(log, "02.inputs/derived/review-fulltext.csv", na = "")
  log |>
    dplyr::filter(!stringr::str_detect(status, "^(held|downloaded|copy)")) |>
    dplyr::transmute(author, year, title, decision, link = dplyr::coalesce(dplyr::if_else(is.na(doi), NA, paste0("https://doi.org/", doi)), url, pdf_url), status) |>
    readr::write_excel_csv("02.inputs/review/raw/pdfs-to-download.csv", na = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-bib
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("04.references/review/review.json")) {
  bib <- readr::read_file("04.references/references.bib")
  held <- tibble::tibble(key = stringr::str_match_all(bib, "@\\w+\\{([^,]+),[^@]*?doi\\s*=\\s*\\{([^}]+)\\}")[[1]][, 2], doi = stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_match_all(bib, "@\\w+\\{([^,]+),[^@]*?doi\\s*=\\s*\\{([^}]+)\\}")[[1]][, 3]))
  dois <- setdiff(stringr::str_to_lower(stats::na.omit(fulltext$doi[fulltext$status != "copy of a work listed above"])), held$doi)
  # CrossRef and DataCite records of each work, by DOI content negotiation, https://citation.crosscite.org/docs.html
  csl <- purrr::map(dois, \(d) tryCatch(httr2::request(paste0("https://doi.org/", d)) |> httr2::req_headers(Accept = "application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json") |> httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 3) |> httr2::req_perform() |> httr2::resp_body_json(), error = \(e) NULL), .progress = TRUE) |>
    purrr::compact() |>
    purrr::map(\(w) w[intersect(names(w), c("type", "title", "author", "editor", "issued", "container-title", "volume", "issue", "page", "DOI", "publisher", "URL"))])
  # CrossRef work types renamed to the item types of the Citation Style Language
  csl_type <- c(`journal-article` = "article-journal", `book-chapter` = "chapter", `posted-content` = "article", `proceedings-article` = "paper-conference", dissertation = "thesis", `peer-review` = "review", `reference-entry` = "entry", `report-component` = "report", monograph = "book", `edited-book` = "book")
  csl <- purrr::map(csl, \(w) purrr::list_modify(w, type = unname(dplyr::coalesce(csl_type[w$type], w$type))))
  # Names kept to their parts and titles to one string, the forms Pandoc reads from CSL JSON
  name_parts <- \(people) purrr::map(people, \(p) p[intersect(names(p), c("family", "given", "literal", "suffix", "non-dropping-particle", "dropping-particle"))]) |>
    purrr::keep(\(p) length(p[intersect(names(p), c("family", "given", "literal"))]) > 0)
  csl <- purrr::map(csl, \(w) {
    w$author <- if (length(w$author)) name_parts(w$author)
    w$editor <- if (length(w$editor)) name_parts(w$editor)
    when <- purrr::keep(w$issued$`date-parts`[[1]], is.numeric)
    w$issued <- if (length(when)) list(`date-parts` = list(when))
    w$title <- unlist(w$title)[1]
    w$`container-title` <- unlist(w$`container-title`)[1]
    w
  })
  minor <- c("from", "with", "what", "does", "into", "their", "this", "that", "under", "over", "using", "toward", "towards", "across", "between", "after", "about", "when", "where", "which")
  first_word <- \(t) purrr::detect(stringr::str_extract_all(stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_remove_all(paste(unlist(t), collapse = " "), "<[^>]+>")), "\\b[a-z]{4,}\\b")[[1]], \(w) !w %in% minor) %||% "work"
  key <- purrr::map_chr(csl, \(w) paste0(stringr::str_remove_all(stringi::stri_trans_general(stringr::str_to_lower(w$author[[1]]$family %||% w$author[[1]]$literal %||% w$publisher %||% "anon"), "Latin-ASCII"), "[^a-z]"),
                                         w$issued$`date-parts`[[1]][[1]] %||% "nd", first_word(w$title)))
  key <- stats::ave(key, key, FUN = \(k) if (length(k) == 1) k else paste0(k, letters[seq_along(k)]))
  stopifnot(!any(key %in% held$key))
  csl <- purrr::map2(csl, key, \(w, k) c(list(id = k), w))
  jsonlite::write_json(csl, "04.references/review/review.json", auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)
  dplyr::bind_rows(held, tibble::tibble(key, doi = stringr::str_to_lower(purrr::map_chr(csl, "DOI")))) |>
    readr::write_csv("04.references/review/review-keys.csv")
}
```

```{r}
kappa <- \(a, b) {
  lv <- c("include", "exclude", "undecided")
  chance <- sum(prop.table(table(factor(a, lv))) * prop.table(table(factor(b, lv))))
  (mean(a == b) - chance) / (1 - chance)
}
```
